title: Software Dev - Need Input on AI Assets
author: Arbetraryday
selftext:
Hello! I am a software engineer and have been for 7 years. Recently I starting making a  3D Cel-Shaded style game but I am not a designer. 

To get to an MVP as a solo dev I completely accept that I need (and have been using) AI for assets, UI and really anything the requires art 😅. If the game does well I will definitely be getting some real designers on board but for now, I will be using AI generation (father, full time job, don't have the money to hire people). 

What tools are you using for assets, rigging, UI design. 

I have some comfy UI workflows and a 5080 (16GB vram) for generation. 

I have been using Trellis, HiDream and now looking into autoriggers. 

Ideally, I would like a workflow that gets me 3D rigged assets for all sorts of forms (humanoid, dragon, canine, etc.)

Any suggestions?

P.S. I don't mind spending time to clean things up in blender if needed, I just don't have the knowledge, time and design skills to create high class assets.

comments.author: That1guy4226
comments.body: I've been looking at Meshy for pretty much the exact same reason.

replies.author: Arbetraryday
replies.body:
I think Meshy has some good stuff going for it, but with potentially hundreds to thousands of assets, it get so expensive and feels harder to automate. I have an items list with Trellis that worked pretty well. Using a python script with comfy UI, it took 16 hours to get through 200 items and they were mostly good for an MVP. 

Obviously items are much less complicated as purely representative and no animation/rigging required. But I was hoping to set something similar up for asset -> rigging -> keyed and organized animations

replies.author: mshort3
replies.body:
I'm in a very similar boat as you, but i'm getting along good with 2d and 3d graphics. 



For meshy, put your art in a 4x4 to 8x8 grid in an image and have meshy make the objects based on that. Split the grid post-processing or in your engine. Meshy makes a grid of good enough medium and lesser sized items in bulk, including texture pass. If you need better textures, pump your gridded image through nano banana prompting for a hq 3d texture pass. 

I'm getting 32-64 items per generation. Meshy has a first month promo where you get like 10k credits (1k gens) letting you get very far.

comments.author: bettertagsweretaken
comments.body: Tripo and Meshy are excellent tools for generating 3D art.

replies.author: Arbetraryday
replies.body: There are so many tutorial on YouTube (thankfully) but I like this guys videos. https://youtube.com/@joeycarlino?si=GDIeHbxjxPA1oV3x

comments.author: nom-nom-babies
comments.body: I have Claude hooked up with a messy API key. Currently learning blender to get good at modifying objects and making more complex systems

replies.author: Arbetraryday
replies.body: Has claude to meshy given valuable outputs?

replies.author: nom-nom-babies
replies.body: The better the descriptions and reference images you give the better. So far it has looked good with my projects. Definitely good for debugging and making characters rigged with skeletons. Your major limitations are going to be objects that have children/subobjects. You will need to create those all separately and scale them or have Claude interface with blender which it can do for basic stuff

comments.author: Firewall0110
comments.body: I've been using claude for both meshy and tripo. Tripo has me paying for credits without a recurring plan and that's been fine. Meshy I paid all upfront for 3000 credits a month for 12 months. Both cases I start with an isometric piece of concept art at fairly highly detail and then use image to model conversion. Tripo is better at hard geometry. Surface details have to be fairly large for meshy 6 to capture appropriately.  I did 45 generations in a batch last night and quality was fine on meshy but not stellar.  Frankly, if you can afford the 30 cents per generation for tripo API, go with that!

comments.author: Chaibi_Alaa
comments.body: Same situation here, 22 y+ as a CTO and recently started learning about this field of gaming. I tried creating my first RTS game with meshy and tripo and many others (custom models on RunPod, confy workflows ..) the issue was always that generated items are too heavy in terms of poly count, and that the generated elements like one block, you don't get for example a building with the window alone, door alone and so so that you can customize them in blender. After multiple and multiple tries, I found out that building elements using blender with claude code and python procedural script is a lot better in terms of customization (not perfect for sure and not for characters).

replies.author: Arbetraryday
replies.body: I didn't even consider the blender/claude code/python combo. Ill have to give that a shot. Thanks!
